headline: Mistakes to Avoid with Clogged Floor Drains
articleBody: A clogged floor drain is a problem that needs attention, but how you address it can make a huge difference. Let's talk about some common blunders and how to steer clear of them. First, don't ignore a slow-draining floor drain. It's often the first symptom of a larger blockage forming down the line, so catch it early! Second, resist the urge to pour corrosive chemical drain cleaners into your floor drain. These products can damage your pipes, especially older ones, and often don't fully clear the blockage. They can also create hazardous fumes and make the situation worse for anyone who eventually has to work on the drain. Third, don't try to use gardening hoses or other inappropriate tools to force water down a clogged drain. This can increase pressure, potentially causing pipes to burst or disconnect, leading to costly leaks. Fourth, assuming the clog will clear itself after a big rain or a few flushes is a gamble. A persistent clog won't disappear and can lead to serious backups. Lastly, don't put off calling a professional if you suspect a significant blockage or if the problem is recurring. Delaying can lead to water damage, mold growth, and more extensive repairs.
